newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria T-bills yield 602 pct after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria T-bills yield 602 pct after rate rise.

text.p: The cumulative annual yield of the Bulgarian Finance Ministry issue of one-year floater coupon T-bills hit 602.46 percent as a new record high interest rate took effect, the central bank said.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said the issue, dated September 25, was 74.8 percent sold at Monday's auction in which five financial institutions took part.
The issue was offered with no minimum acceptable price set in advance by the ministry and bears a coupon equal to the BNB's central interest rate (CIR) for the period to maturity.
The BNB raised the CIR to a historic high 300 percent annually from 108 percent, effective Tuesday, in a bid to restore confidence in the slumping national currency, the lev.

But the 300 percent CIR could put an additional burden on the budget because the yields of most of Bulgaria's floater coupon T-bills now in circulation change in line with the BNB's main rate, experts said.
BNB governor Lybomir Filipov said the record high CIR might be considered a temporary measure.
